item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00120","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C01","C17"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 supplies the child’s distinctive termination machinery and nearly verbatim operative language: prior trade-agreement proclamations are made ineffective while preserving provisions concerning termination on six months’ notice. The child adapts that same structure from earlier Cuban agreements to the 1935 Brazilian agreement. C01 is also closely connected and supplies the immediate GATT/Brazil contracting-party predicate, but its operative provisions concern activating concessions rather than terminating an older agreement. C17 is a weaker contextual model from the same section 350/GATT proclamation series.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"said proclamation of December 2, 1935 shall not be in effect after July 30, 1948 except insofar as it relates to the termination on six months' notice of said trade agreement","parent_excerpt":"each of the proclamations specified in the 12th, 13th, and 14th recitals of this proclamation shall not be in effect after December 31, 1947, except insofar as it may relate to the termination on six months' notice of any of the exclusive trade agreements","explanation":"This is distinctive, nearly verbatim operative language implementing the same mechanism: deactivate an earlier trade-agreement proclamation while preserving its six-month termination right."},{"child_excerpt":"except the right of termination thereof on six months' notice, shall be inoperative","parent_excerpt":"except the right of termination on one year's notice of said convention and on six months' notice of said exclusive trade agreement of August 24, 1934, as amended, shall become inoperative","explanation":"The recitals share the same legal structure and phrasing, preserving termination rights while declaring the underlying earlier agreement inoperative."},{"child_excerpt":"acting under the authority conferred by the said section 350(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended","parent_excerpt":"acting under the authority of said section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended","explanation":"Both invoke the same statutory authority as part of the closely parallel operative framework; in combination with the distinctive termination language, this supports direct template reuse rather than mere topical similarity."}]}
